reporting_issues.note: Table 1 footnote e and 3.2 (p. 4); 1239 / 1014 = 1.22, so about a fifth more.

Supported by the review's own numbers although it never states its unit of analysis: Table 3 uses 15664 samples and 119680 pills as N, and Table 4 gives single-trial intervals that person-level data could not produce (urine RR 0.80, 0.71 to 0.90, for Das et al., 2010, 30 participants; adherence RR 0.94, 0.92 to 0.96, for Heinzerling et al., 2013, 19 participants; adherence 0.95, 0.91 to 1.00, for Das et al.).

Table 4 (p. 9): 0.85 (0.78, 0.93) for the four 12-week trials vs 0.90 (0.81, 1.00) with Heinzerling 2013 added; 0.92 (0.89, 0.94) for Trivedi's two stages vs 0.98 (0.89, 1.08) with Heinzerling 2013 added.
2.6 (p. 3) and the reference list (p. 11) cite RoB 2 as Higgins et al. (2011); 'Medium' in Table 3 (p. 7) and 3.4.7 (p. 8); Table S1 cited as Appendix 8 in 3.4.4 (p. 6) and as Appendix 10 elsewhere.

risk_of_bias.note: AMSTAR 2 is the right instrument and I agree with every item except item 4. Item 4 (critical) should be no, not partial yes: AMSTAR 2's partial yes requires all of at least two databases, keywords or a strategy, and justified publication restrictions, and reports were limited to seven languages (2.3, p. 2) with no justification; the limit excludes, for example, Chinese-, Japanese-, Korean- and Thai-language reports. With item 11 also not met, there are two critical flaws, so the overall is critically low confidence, provisional while item 7 rests on the unread Appendix 5. The project's cards read item 4 two ways (sc_sibanda_2019 and sc_siefried_2020 score an unjustified language limit as no; sc_mcketin_2019, sc_cohenlaroque_2024 and sc_voce_2019 as partial yes); the senior author should fix one reading. Under the lenient reading the card's low confidence (provisional) stands.

risk_of_bias_domains.note: Registered 7 October 2022 (2.1, p. 2), before the search window closed; protocol content (Appendix 1) not read, so partial yes rather than yes.

Unjustified restriction to seven languages (2.3, p. 2) fails the partial-yes criterion; everything else in the search is strong (seven databases, six registries, grey literature, reference lists, librarian-designed and PRESS-reviewed strategies).

interpretation_gap.note: Minor is defensible: the Abstract and Conclusion carry the very-low rating and call the effect modest and its relevance unverified. The main overreach is the Abstract's closing sentence, which presents two subgroup results (larger in males for craving, larger with longer treatment for use) without the Discussion's caveats (one men-only trial at high risk of bias; duration confounded with medication and population).

missed: The trials are more interlinked than the card says. Bakouni's reference list (pp. 11–12) shows Steven Shoptaw as an author of five trials (six of the seven urine reports: Das 2010, Heinzerling 2013 and 2014, Shoptaw 2008, both Trivedi 2021 stages); the seventh urine report, Elkashef 2008, shares Walter Ling with Shoptaw 2008 and Trivedi 2021 and eight NIDA authors (Elkashef, Anderson, Li, Holmes, Chiang, Kahn, Campbell, Haning) with Anderson 2015. Only Ghoreishi 2017 (Iran) has no author link to the others, and it gave no urine data. No urine report is independent of the others.

Retention count: Table 2 (p. 6) marks retention as available for eight reports, including both Trivedi stages, but 3.4.2 and Table 3 pool seven reports with 786 participants; 786 equals the six bupropion-alone trials with retention data plus Trivedi stage 2 (561 + 225, editors' calculation from Table 1), and Table 4 lists one 450-mg report for retention. One Trivedi stage (apparently stage 1, 403 people) was left out without comment.

Table 4 marks the bupropion-alone urine estimate, 0.90 (0.81, 1.00), as individually significant (asterisk, P < 0.05), so the review counts it as a significant reduction; at the printed precision the interval reaches 1, and under the unit-of-analysis problem a person-level interval would be wider.
The Discussion says Trivedi et al. combined bupropion with naloxone (p. 10); the trial used injectable naltrexone (Table 1 footnote c, p. 5). Typo, no consequence.
Table 4 footnote 3 lists three trials (Das, Elkashef, Shoptaw) for the mixed-use-frequency urine subgroup printed with N = 5; the other two must be Trivedi's stages. Minor.
